notes:
- A profile's saved copy survives a cache wipe: The bio, the banner and avatar URLs, the favourites, the totals and the list were snapshotted under the app's cache directory, which Android empties whenever it wants the space back - and "Clear cache" empties on request. So the app kept forgetting a profile it had already read, and downloaded every part of it again. The snapshots live in private app storage now, and the first launch after the change adopts the directory the old builds wrote, so nobody pays for it with a fresh download.
- A bio is parsed once, not twice: The profile screen parses a bio to find the AniList links whose posters it fetches, and the About card parses the same text to draw it. Both threw the result away, so every open walked the same Markdown twice. A bounded cache now holds parsed bios for the session, keyed on the document itself, and a reopened profile parses nothing.
- The bio's posters stop blinking on every open: Each profile publishes twice - the saved copy, then the live overview - and both carried the same bio. The second publish cancelled the first poster batch, emptied the map and asked for the identical keys again, so every inline cover on the page disappeared and came back for a request that was already in flight. A bio that has been answered is left alone now, and a refresh with no bio edit asks for nothing.
- A long bio reads its document once per frame: "Show more" needs to know whether a bio is worth collapsing, and the card asked that question twice on every composition - two full walks of the parsed document, including a recursive search for images, while the expand animates the card on every frame. It is asked once and remembered.
- A full cover cache evicts its oldest covers, not all of them: The in-memory cover cache cleared itself the moment it reached its ceiling. One bio with a dozen links on top of a media page was enough to trip it, and every profile opened afterwards re-asked for posters whose URLs were still in its snapshot. It drops expired entries first and then the oldest ones, so what stays is what the reader is most likely to come back to.
- A banner opens at its real height the second time: The header sizes itself from the banner picture, and that measurement only arrives with the decoded image - so every open, including one whose banner was already on disk, drew the landscape placeholder and animated to the real height a moment later. The last measured size is remembered per URL, so a revisit is laid out correctly on its first frame.
- The banner and avatar go through the disk cache by name: Both were handed to the image loader as bare URLs, rebuilt on every recomposition, with the disk entry left to whatever the default key happened to be. They carry explicit keys and read/write cache policies now, so the portrait and the artwork are kept next to the covers and a revisit draws them without a request. A changed portrait or banner is a new AniList URL, so stale artwork is unrepresentable.
- The profile's waiting state is shaped like its header: A cold open drew a centred spinner where the page was about to be, and the header then arrived as a jump. The waiting state now sketches the one shape every profile shares - banner, avatar on its edge, name, the two list counts, the summary strip and the About card - with the message underneath, and stops before the favourites row that may or may not exist.
- The credits page shows itsmechinmoy's own animated portrait: Every helper's card drew a GitHub avatar. Chimnoy's row now uses the animated portrait he uses in Dartotsu's developer list, pinned as his own URL rather than re-hosted, so his face moves while the other names stay still. It is the one animated image on the page, and it is only on his row.
- The card preview prints a caption only where the Library does: Shelf never prints a title under its covers in the Library, and the card-design preview printed one anyway - a picture of a page the reader would not get. The caption rule now lives on the Library view itself, and the grid and both Settings previews read that one answer.
- Mosaic previews as a mosaic: Mosaic's whole difference from Big cards is the full-width cover every third cell, and the card-design preview drew it as a flat two-up grid. It now draws the landscape anchor over the pair, at the proportion the Library gives the hero, so the two modes no longer preview alike.
- Grouped covers previews its status heading: Grouped covers sorts the poster grid under status headings; the preview drew the grid without them, which made the mode look like the plain poster grid beside it. The preview now opens with the heading the Library prints above the covers.
- The Compact grid preview keeps its names: The layout preview drew the Compact grid caption-free while the Library prints a name under every compact cover. All four poster modes in that preview now ask the mode whether it prints a caption, so choosing a density no longer shows a page that does not exist.
Build 693.
